objective.statement: Name the voices of a choir and put the voice types in order of height.
successCriteria: I know soprano, alto, tenor and bass are the four choral voices.
I know mezzo-soprano lies between soprano and alto, and baritone between tenor and bass.
I can tell a very high or very low part from its notes.

explanation.text: Choral music is usually written for four voices, from the highest to the lowest: soprano, alto, tenor and bass (SATB). Women and children often sing soprano and alto; men often sing tenor and bass.

Singers, especially solo singers, are also described by ranges in between. The mezzo-soprano lies between the soprano and the alto. The baritone lies between the tenor and the bass. So the six voices, from the highest to the lowest, are soprano, mezzo-soprano, alto, tenor, baritone, bass.

music.textAlternative: Four crotchets high in the treble stave: E, F, G, A.

explanation.caption: A part as high as this suits a soprano.

music.textAlternative: Four crotchets low in the bass stave: E, F, G, A.

explanation.caption: A part as low as this suits a bass.

explanation.text: You can often tell a part from its notes. A part that lies wholly above the highest note an alto can comfortably sing is a soprano part; one that lies wholly below the lowest note of a tenor is a bass part. In between, the ranges overlap, so you will only be asked about the very high and the very low.
High to low: soprano, (mezzo-soprano), alto, tenor, (baritone), bass. Mezzo and baritone are the in-between voices.

steps: The notes are all high in the treble stave.
They lie above the comfortable top of an alto.
So the part is for a soprano.
